support.title: Swelling and weight changes
support.text: Report swelling early and discuss changes in weight, movement or breathing. The team will assess the cause and agree treatment; do not start a water tablet or change tepotinib yourself.

support.title: Diarrhoea and fluids
support.text: Agree a diarrhoea treatment plan before starting. Begin the prescribed anti-diarrhoeal medicine at the first loose stool as instructed, and maintain fluids if able. Persistent diarrhoea, weakness or reduced urine needs prompt advice.

support.title: Nausea medicines
support.text: Tepotinib has minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Agree an as-needed anti-sickness plan with the team, including medicine-interaction and heart-rhythm checks; no routine infusion premedication is specified.

support.title: Medicine review
support.text: Ask the pharmacist to check all prescribed medicines, non-prescription medicines and supplements before changes. Tepotinib can affect medicines including dabigatran, digoxin, rosuvastatin and metformin. Supportive medicines may also affect heart rhythm; individual advice is needed.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
support.text: Avoid pregnancy during treatment. Effective contraception is needed during treatment and for at least one week after the last dose; women using hormonal contraception should also use a barrier method. Men with a partner who could become pregnant should use barrier contraception for the same period. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least one week afterwards. Human fertility effects are not known; discuss fertility before starting.

questions.q: Is this a fixed course of chemotherapy?
questions.a: No. These targeted tablets are taken daily without a planned rest week, while they are helping and your team considers treatment appropriate.

questions.q: Why does a trial mention 500 mg?
questions.a: The VISION trial’s 500 mg salt dose corresponds to 450 mg active tepotinib. The prescribed tablets contain 225 mg active tepotinib each; follow your own prescription.

questions.q: What if I forget or vomit a dose?
questions.a: Take a forgotten dose when remembered on the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip it. Never double up. Ask your pharmacist about vomiting or uncertain timing before taking any replacement.

questions.q: Why might my creatinine test change?
questions.a: Tepotinib can change how creatinine is handled by the kidneys, but real kidney problems can also occur. The team must assess the change; neither explanation should be assumed.

questions.q: Can I change the dose when I feel better?
questions.a: Only your team can authorise restarting or changing the dose after side effects. Feeling better does not establish that blood tests or other checks have recovered.

drug_mechanisms.tepotinib: Reversible ATP-competitive MET tyrosine kinase inhibitor; suppresses MET phosphorylation and downstream PI3K/Akt and MAPK/ERK signalling in tumours with activating MET alterations.

items.text: Take whole capsules with or without food; do not crush or chew. Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit products and Seville oranges. items.text: Give the team a complete medicine and supplement list, including St John’s wort. CYP3A inhibitors/inducers and medicines affecting heart rhythm need pharmacy review. Do not change the cancer dose yourself; temporary interaction doses differ from toxicity reductions.

items.text: Ask pharmacy for the approved method. Current SmPC allows capsule suspension and enteral administration; the older NCCP says not to open capsules. Instructions and vomiting advice depend on the formulation.

items.title: Thinking, vision and driving
items.text: Do not drive or use machinery while experiencing dizziness, fainting, blurred vision or cognitive effects. Ask family/supporters to report noticeable memory or behaviour changes.

items.title: Bones and falls
items.text: New focal pain, changed gait or mobility needs prompt review for a fracture; reduce fall hazards where possible.

items.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
items.text: Avoid pregnancy. Women who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least five weeks afterwards; add a barrier method if using systemic hormonal contraception. Men with partners who could become pregnant need highly effective contraception during treatment and for at least three months afterwards. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility and family plans before starting.

sections.text: Take at the same time daily without food: leave at least 3 hours after food before the dose and wait at least 1 hour afterwards before eating. Swallow with water. If missed, take it the same day unless the next dose is due within 8 hours; then skip. Never double a dose or repeat a vomited dose. Ask pharmacy for the approved water-dispersion method if swallowing is difficult.

sections.title: Supplies and visits
sections.text: Arrange the next prescription before tablets run out. Keep your blood-test and clinic appointments. The oral regimen itself does not require an infusion line or pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held

sections.title: At treatment change

evidence.title: Evidence for this treatment setting
evidence.intro: The mutation and prior treatment matter.
evidence.population: EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC · EGFR-TKI-naïve
evidence.interpretation: In studies of selected EGFR-mutated advanced lung cancers, afatinib delayed cancer progression compared with cisplatin/pemetrexed. The overall survival comparison in that trial was not statistically significant. A separate comparison with gefitinib also did not show a statistically significant overall-survival difference. Ask how the study population and alternatives match your situation.

support.title: Diarrhoea and fluids
support.text: Keep prescribed anti-diarrhoea medicine available from the first dose. Start your agreed plan at the first loose stool, keep drinking if able and report symptoms early. Your team may advise continuing symptom medicine until loose stools have stopped for 12 hours. Severe diarrhoea, weakness or reduced urine needs urgent advice.

support.title: Skin, nails and mouth
support.text: Use the agreed EGFR-inhibitor skin-care and mouth-care plan. Emollients and sun protection may help; report rash, painful nails or mouth sores early. The team decides whether creams, antibiotics or other treatment are needed.

support.title: Nausea medicines
support.text: Afatinib has minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Routine infusion premedication is not required. Agree any as-needed anti-sickness medicine with the team, after checking interactions and your medical history.

support.title: Medicine interactions
support.text: Give pharmacy a list of all medicines, herbal products and supplements. Some P-gp inhibitors need separated dosing; strong inducers such as St John’s wort can reduce afatinib exposure. Ask for a written individual schedule before adding or changing medicines.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
support.text: Avoid pregnancy. Women who could become pregnant need adequate contraception during treatment and for at least 1 month after the final dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility and future pregnancy plans before starting.

items.text: Call urgently for new or worsening breathlessness, cough or fever; severe diarrhoea, inability to drink or much less urine; severe or persistent abdominal pain; blistering or peeling skin; or yellow skin/eyes. clinical.component_rationale: Afatinib is an irreversible EGFR-family tyrosine kinase inhibitor. It interrupts signals involved in cancer-cell growth; the tumour mutation test and treatment setting determine whether it is suitable.
key_points: Keep EGFR-TKI-naïve NCCP scope separate from licensed squamous post-platinum disease.
Grade 2 diarrhoea >48 hours or rash >7 days, intolerable grade 2, or grade ≥3: hold until grade 0/1, then discuss a 10 mg reduction.
Suspected ILD: hold and investigate; confirmed ILD: permanently stop. Pre-existing ILD is an NCCP exclusion.
NCCP CrCl <15/dialysis and Child–Pugh C recommendations conflict with EMA restrictions; no automatic dose is supplied.

items.title: Diarrhoea and fluids
items.text: Keep prescribed anti-diarrhoea medicine available from the first dose. Start your agreed plan at the first loose stool, keep drinking if able and report symptoms early. items.text: Use the agreed EGFR-inhibitor skin-care and mouth-care plan. Emollients and sun protection may help; report rash, painful nails or mouth sores early. The team decides whether creams, antibiotics or other treatment are needed.

items.title: Nausea medicines
items.text: Dacomitinib has minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Routine infusion premedication is not required. Agree any as-needed anti-sickness medicine with the team, after checking interactions and your medical history.

items.title: Medicine interactions
items.text: Acid-suppressing medicines can reduce dacomitinib exposure. Proton pump inhibitors should be avoided if possible; ask pharmacy about alternatives. NCCP and current product information give different timing before H2 blockers, so obtain a written individual schedule. CYP2D6 medicines also need pharmacy review. Do not change medicines yourself.

items.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
items.text: Avoid pregnancy. Women who could become pregnant need adequate contraception during treatment and for at least 17 days after the final dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility and future pregnancy plans before starting.

chapters.title: When to get urgent help
chapters.intro: Do not wait for the next appointment.

items.title: Call urgently

Eye pain, light sensitivity or blurred vision needs prompt assessment. Severe breathing difficulty, collapse or swelling of the tongue/throat needs emergency help. Use your unit’s temperature and 24-hour contact instructions.

items.title: When you call
items.text: Give the medicine name, last dose and symptoms. Tell the team if you can drink, pass urine and manage usual activities. Do not delay calling while gathering information.

chapters.title: What studies tell us
chapters.intro: In a study of previously untreated advanced lung cancer with common EGFR mutations, dacomitinib delayed progression and improved overall survival compared with gefitinib. The study excluded people with a history of brain or other central nervous system metastases. It did not compare dacomitinib with every treatment available today. Group results cannot predict your own outcome.

evidence.limitations: TAX317 was a historical randomised study after platinum chemotherapy; it predates current targeted therapy and immunotherapy. questions.q: What benefit is realistic for me and what other options are available?
questions.a: Treatment aims to control small-cell lung cancer after previous therapy and may help symptoms. The evidence is limited, so discuss likely benefit, burdens and alternatives with the team. A small uncontrolled study found some tumour responses to weekly paclitaxel in previously treated SCLC. The study used six weekly doses followed by two weeks without treatment, which differs from this NCCP schedule. It cannot establish a survival advantage over other treatment or supportive care.

evidence.interpretation: Discuss possible benefit, alternatives and uncertainty for your own situation. The treatment aim is cancer control and symptom relief.
evidence.limitations: Yamamoto 2006 enrolled 22 patients, with 21 eligible; it was a small single-arm phase II study without a control group. The trial schedule was 80 mg/m² weekly for six weeks of an eight-week cycle, not the NCCP Day 1/8/15/22 28-day schedule or its three-of-four-week alternative. Five partial responses were observed: three of 11 sensitive and two of 10 refractory cases. These counts are not a comparative efficacy estimate. The study cannot establish a survival benefit, modern treatment ranking or the expected response probability for the current NCCP schedule. NCCP explicitly flags 00226d as off-label; publication and NCCP listing do not create an Irish product licence.

anatomy: White blood cells can fall, raising the risk of infection. Anaemia can cause tiredness or breathlessness; low platelets can cause bruising or bleeding. Blood tests guide delays and dose changes. Fever, shaking chills or feeling suddenly unwell need the oncology emergency contact immediately.

The bowel can slow down and nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or sore mouth can occur. Use the prescribed bowel and anti-sickness plan. Severe abdominal pain, swelling, repeated vomiting or inability to pass stool/gas needs urgent assessment for ileus; do not simply take extra laxatives.
Nerve effects may change sensation, grip, walking or bowel movement. Report changes early because the next dose may need to wait or be reduced.
Tiredness, hair thinning/loss and liver-test changes can occur. Pace activities and tell the team if eating, drinking or daily tasks become difficult.
New chest pain, sudden or worsening breathlessness, or severe allergic symptoms need urgent medical help. Previous heart disease and interacting medicines need review before treatment.
Tell staff immediately about burning, pain, swelling or leakage.

questions.q: Can IV and oral vinorelbine be exchanged?
questions.a: Oral 60/80 mg/m² and IV 25/30 mg/m² have pharmacokinetic equivalence references, but never convertmg-for-mg or swap routes yourself. Dose rules and schedules differ.

questions.q: How long will treatment continue?
questions.a: Continue weekly while helpful and tolerated; no fixed total number of weeks.

questions.q: Do I need regular heart scans?
questions.a: Review cardiovascular history and new symptoms. These monotherapy NCCP protocols do not mandate the serial LVEF/echo schedule used for anthracyclines or trastuzumab; arrange cardiac tests when clinically indicated.

questions.q: What if I vomit, miss a dose or find damaged capsules?
questions.a: Do not take another dose if vomiting occurs within a few hours. Contact the team and record the dose taken. Do not swallow damaged capsules. Return them to pharmacy; immediately wash any contact with contents using water or saline. Missed/late dose: contact the team for the next date. Do not double or move the weekly schedule yourself. This is pragmatic medication-safety advice, not an extra NCCP catch-up schedule.

questions.q: How do I store the capsules?
questions.a: Current Vinorelbine Accord SmPC: refrigerator 2–8°C. Confirm the dispensed brand/pack instructions; keep in original packaging and out of children’s reach. Return unused or damaged capsules to pharmacy; follow cytotoxic handling advice.

questions.q: Does dose four always use more capsules?
questions.a: No. The team reviews the lowest counts and side effects after the first three doses. Take only the current prescribed dose; severe or repeated low counts can prevent an increase.

anatomy: White blood cells can fall, raising the risk of infection. Anaemia can cause tiredness or breathlessness; low platelets can cause bruising or bleeding. Blood tests guide delays and dose changes. Fever, shaking chills or feeling suddenly unwell need the oncology emergency contact immediately.

The bowel can slow down and nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea or sore mouth can occur. Use the prescribed bowel and anti-sickness plan. Severe abdominal pain, swelling, repeated vomiting or inability to pass stool/gas needs urgent assessment for ileus; do not simply take extra laxatives.
Nerve effects may change sensation, grip, walking or bowel movement. Report changes early because the next dose may need to wait or be reduced.
Tiredness, hair thinning/loss and liver-test changes can occur. Pace activities and tell the team if eating, drinking or daily tasks become difficult.
New chest pain, sudden or worsening breathlessness, or severe allergic symptoms need urgent medical help. Previous heart disease and interacting medicines need review before treatment.

milestones.title: Confirm treatment scope
milestones.when: Before starting and whenever the partner changes
milestones.why: NCCP 00215f: first-line unresectable advanced, recurrent or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with platinum-based chemotherapy. NCCP 00215g: the corresponding first-line EGFR-activating-mutation setting with erlotinib. This is the bevacizumab component; every partner needs its own prescription, assessment and consent.
milestones.clinical: Platinum has up to six combined cycles before bevacizumab continuation. Erlotinib is not governed by this six-cycle cap.
milestones.action: Confirm indication, partner, phase and separate assessment.

milestones.title: Blood pressure and proteinuria
milestones.when: Baseline, each cycle and extra checks when indicated
milestones.why: These effects can be silent, so attend planned tests even when well.
milestones.clinical: Apply BP persistence/control and quantified 24-hour protein rules; distinguish g/L from g/24 h.
milestones.action: Agree who books, reviews and acts on each test.

milestones.title: Procedures and urgent symptoms
milestones.why: Seek urgent help for sudden severe abdominal pain, significant bleeding or coughing blood, chest pain, breathlessness, a swollen painful leg, a severe headache, confusion, seizures, a change in vision, or a rapidly painful/red spreading wound. Follow the chemotherapy emergency plan for fever or feeling acutely unwell.
milestones.clinical: Surgery and wound-healing criteria can override routine cycle timing; no automatic restart from the calendar.
milestones.action: Contact the team before procedures or for urgent symptoms.

clinical_notes: This is a shared bevacizumab component protocol; companion chemotherapy or other SACT is not assessed by these rules.

NCCP 00215 v7 states renal/hepatic impairment has not been studied and supplies no validated adjustment. Review initial organ eligibility and clinical suitability with the consultant; do not import 00212 v7 organ-function permission.

NCCP BP notation >150/100 and >200/110 does not explicitly state how to combine isolated systolic and diastolic abnormalities. A clinician confirms uncontrolled/severe BP; no invented binary calculation is used.
Grade 3 hypertension requires persistence before source discontinuation applies. A new grade 3 event alone is not encoded as a permanent-stop criterion.
NCCP grades in the bevacizumab toxicity table do not identify a CTCAE edition. Existing interface CTCAE v5 descriptions are orientation aids; source grading must be confirmed.
Normal proteinuria results do not clear unassessed blood pressure, surgical, bleeding or partner-treatment domains.
NCCP 00215 v7 retains initial numeric blood-count and organ eligibility. These are not a cycle-by-cycle bevacizumab dose-modification algorithm.
Relative educational stages only; no patient-entered dates.
The ovarian 15-month/22-cycle cap does not apply to lung treatment.
ECOG 4599 and JO25567 evidence belongs to different selected populations and partners.

support_plans.label: Bevacizumab lung component · support plan
additional_support: Bevacizumab itself usually needs no routine anti-sickness premedication. Platinum chemotherapy needs its own anti-sickness and other support plan. Erlotinib needs its own tablet, interaction, skin and diarrhoea plan. Keep the complete plan and emergency numbers.
No routine bevacizumab antiemetic prophylaxis; assess partner chemotherapy emetic risk separately.
Anti-diarrhoeal medicines only if required under local policy.
Maintain BP/urine, procedure/wound and urgent-contact plans.
At the platinum-to-bevacizumab continuation change, review and stop or adapt partner-specific support only on the prescriber’s instruction. Erlotinib support continues according to its own plan.
